title: Scope of Supervised Fine-Tuning
summary: Work through Scope of Supervised Fine-Tuning.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Scope of Supervised Fine-Tuning**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Fine-Tuning, § Scope of Supervised Fine-Tuning
blocks.md: Before turning an admitted record such as `trace_r19_01_redacted_v1` into a weight update, engineers must decide whether the failure it repaired belongs in the model's parameters at all. Fine-tuning a model to work around a missing prompt instruction or a broken tool schema bakes a temporary workaround into billions of weights, only for the behavior to break again the next time the interface changes. Modifying model weights is an expensive, high-blast-radius change reserved for behavioral failures that survive cheaper fixes.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Three homes for behavior matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Fine-tuning changes only the proposal distribution, so stable procedure can move into weights, deployment-varying contracts stay in context, and enforcement stays in the runtime.

questions.q: The section **Scope of Supervised Fine-Tuning** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Fine-tuning changes only the proposal distribution, so stable procedure can move into weights, deployment-varying contracts stay in context, and enforcement stays in the runtime.

A disagreement rate measured on reference prefixes bounds excess task cost only by min(H, H^2 eps), while the same rate on learner states with bounded recovery cost gives a linear bound, so where imitation error is measured sets the horizon penalty.
LoRA cuts trainable parameters but parameter state falls only by the byte ratio of trainable to frozen state, and adapters give modularity, not isolation.

Loss is placed only on selected policy-response positions while prompts, refused proposals, and observations stay as attended context with zero loss, because a trajectory has two authors and only one is trained.
